_comment: Pinned upstream digests for the Linux sidecars (Aether core and Xray routing
engine) used by the Linux desktop build.
The release archives and their .sha256 companions live at the same base URL, so
verifying an archive against the checksum file beside it proves only that the
transfer was intact - anyone able to replace the release can replace both. These
values are committed here so the expected digest comes from this repository at
review time rather than from the server being verified.
Provenance for the Aether archives: the asset digests GitHub itself reports
through the releases API for tag v1.9.0 (published 2026-09-04T17:17:48Z), which
is a different source from the release's own .sha256 files. These are the same
API-sourced values already pinned for the Windows and Android archives in the
sibling entries of aether-pins.json.
'binary' records the SHA-256 of the executable extracted from each archive. The
Linux fetch script derives them at fetch time and refuses to proceed unless the
outer archive digest matched first, so the extracted-bin pin inherits the
archive's trust; both are then re-checked on disk. These trimmed-down binaries
are what src-tauri/src/process.rs (AETHER_SHA256) and
src-tauri/src/routing.rs (XRAY_SHA256) refuse to launch without.
The Linux core exposes exactly the same Aether v1.9.0 build the Windows client
ships, compiled for x86_64/aarch64/armv7 against a static musl libc so a single
artifact runs on every Linux distribution of that CPU family (glibc and musl,
systemd and otherwise). The core is a SOCKS5 provider; system-wide routing in
VPN Mode is performed by the bundled Xray engine's TUN, exactly as on Windows,
with the Linux route/DNS programming delegated to an `iproute2` helper behind a
polkit/sudo prompt.
Updating a version means changing its version and every digest in one reviewed
commit, and updating the matching constants in process.rs / routing.rs.
